title: Security incidents are priced into a Prime's borrow rate and insurance fees rather than only punished administratively
content:
Two provisions turn the Incident Registry into a financial input. A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.4.2.1: "the Registry shall serve as a critical input to the Prime Agent Credit Rating system and will determine Primes' Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate when variable pricing is activated." A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.4.2.2: insurance-related fees charged by a Prime's Operational Executor "shall also be calculated using risk-based pricing informed by the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry, including the severity, frequency, and recency of incidents."

A one-off fine is a bounded, budgetable cost that a well-capitalized actor can absorb as a licence fee for sloppiness. Pricing incidents into the borrow rate makes the consequence *continuous and proportional to activity*: a Prime with a poor security record pays more for every unit of capital it deploys, for as long as the record is recent.

The inclusion of **recency** matters as much as severity and frequency. It supplies a rehabilitation gradient — the penalty decays with clean operation — which keeps the mechanism from becoming a permanent brand and preserves the incentive to improve after a bad quarter.

Structurally this is the Atlas doing alignment engineering rather than rule enforcement: it narrows the gap between what is cheap and what is safe, so a Prime's self-interested cost minimization pushes toward better security process without anyone needing to police it case by case.
description: The Registry feeds the Prime Agent Credit Rating and risk-based insurance pricing weighted by severity, frequency and recency — converting process compliance into an ongoing cost of capital.
